title: Put a seated care manikin's feet on a wheelchair's footplates: lift each limp leg, fold its plate down, lower the foot
instruction: The resident manikin has just been seated in the wheelchair. Fold both footplates down and put its feet on them, then let go.
context: Nursing assistants (O*NET 31-1131.00; 1,505,900 employed in 2025) "transport patients to treatment units, testing units, operating rooms, or other areas, using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds". Every transfer into a wheelchair ends the same way: the footplates were folded up or swung aside so the person could get in, and before the chair is moved each foot has to be on its plate. A nursing school's transfer checklist has both steps: "Move footrests out of the way or remove them if possible" and, once the patient is seated, "Position the patient in proper body alignment with feet supported on footrests". A resident who cannot lift a leg needs it done for them. A limp lower leg hangs where the plate has to come down and does not stay where it is put, so one hand lifts and holds the leg while the other folds the plate down under it. The plate must not be let fall against the leg, and the leg must not be dropped.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table top. The table (far edge at x 91) and a fixed board of the same height behind it (70 x 130 cm) stand in for the floor. Wheelchair, fixed (wheel locks on), facing the robot: a standard adult folding manual wheelchair, steel tube frame, black sling seat and back; seat 18 x 16 in (45.7 x 40.6 cm), 19.5 in (49.5 cm) above the floor; back 16 in; 8 in (20.3 cm) casters; 24 in (61 cm) rear wheels; 34 in (86 cm) deep without footrests. The middle of the seat's front edge is at x 72.5, y 0 (layout B: x 74.5, y 1.5). Its swing-away footrests are in place: each hanger tube runs from the frame's front post, 46 up, forward and down to x 59.5, 18.5 up, at y +-22.9. Two flip-up footplates, black composite, 15.2 x 15.2 x 1.2 cm (6 x 6 in), 250 g, each hinged along its outer edge (y +-20.0, x 47.3 to 62.5). Folded down a plate is level with its top 16.0 up and reaches in to y +-4.8. Both start folded up, standing 5 degrees past upright against a stop; pushed past upright a plate falls onto its down stop by itself. Manikin: an adult care manikin 58 in (147 cm) tall, about 28 lb, with jointed knees (KERi Complete Nursing Skills Manikin, LF04020), in a light blue gown, seated with its hips against the back, thighs level, hands on its thighs. For real trials a lower-cost stand-in is specified in the README ("Building the legs", with a drawing): two jointed lower legs of timber, plastic tube and foam on a seat board strapped to the chair, with the same knee positions, leg and foot sizes, 780 g and free knees; nothing in the task touches the manikin above the knees. Knees at x 66.0, 55.0 up, y +-11.0; the manikin's right leg is on the robot's left. Each lower leg hangs free on its knee hinge (20 degrees back to 85 forward): knee to sole 39.5, bare foot 22.2 long and 8.4 wide, heel 4.4 behind the shank's axis, 780 g with the foot, ankle splinted at a right angle. The feet hang with toes toward the robot (toe tips near x 48), soles 15.5 up: 5 mm lower than the tops of the plates will be, and in the plates' way. Both arms start in their rest pose.
scoring: Scored at the end, each side by itself, the two added (a side photo with a protractor, a ruler, the video). A side scores 0 while its footplate is not down on its stop (within 5 degrees of level). It also scores 0 if its plate touched that leg (came within 2 mm of it) at any time while the plate was not down: a plate folded onto a foot that still hangs, or leaned on the leg. Otherwise 0.25: the plate is down. 0.5 instead: the plate is down and the foot rests on it (the middle of the heel's pad, 3 cm in front of the heel's back, and the middle of the foot, both on the sole's midline, are over the plate's top, and the sole's lowest point is no more than 5 mm above it), both grippers are at least 3 cm from that leg, and leg and plate are at rest (turning under 5 degrees a second). So the totals are 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0. The whole trial scores 0 if a knee ever turns faster than 90 degrees a second (the leg was jerked or dropped), or a lower leg is taken more than 80 degrees forward of hanging or more than 15 degrees back (forced). Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Lift each foot off its plate, fold both plates up against their stops and let the legs hang until they are still. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size. Each lower leg is one rigid piece on a knee hinge: the ankle is rigid at a right angle, thighs and trunk are fixed, and the leg cannot move sideways, so it has to be lifted about 50 degrees for the plate to pass under it. The chair is fixed (wheel locks on); only its two footplates move. Estimates, not measurements: leg mass, leg and foot sizes, knee and hinge friction, plate size and mass, the footrests' shape. Not tried on a physical rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (the demo video shows the left wrist, overhead and right wrist cameras side by side; the setup picture shows the overhead camera beside a wrist-camera view taken with the right arm raised)
